name: Saint James the Apostle
dates: Died c. 44 · Galilee, Jerusalem and Compostela
history: James, son of Zebedee and brother of Saint John, was a fisherman whom Christ called from his nets. With Peter and John he saw the Transfiguration and the agony in the garden. He was the first of the Twelve to die for Christ, beheaded by Herod Agrippa in Jerusalem. Tradition links him with Spain and his shrine at Compostela.
life: Christ found James and John mending nets in their father’s boat, and they left him with the hired men and followed. He called the brothers Boanerges, sons of thunder, perhaps for their temper: they once wanted to call down fire on a Samaritan village that would not receive Him. Their mother asked that they might sit at His right and left in His kingdom, and Christ asked whether they could drink His cup. James said they could, and he did. Around the year 44 Herod Agrippa I had him put to the sword, the only death of an apostle recorded in the New Testament. A tradition holds that James had preached in Spain and that his body was brought there. In the ninth century a tomb believed to be his was found in Galicia, and Santiago de Compostela became, with Rome and Jerusalem, one of the great pilgrimages of Christendom. Pilgrims still walk the Camino, with the scallop shell as their sign.
prayerTo: Saint James, son of thunder, you promised to drink the cup of Christ and you kept your word with your life. Pray for pilgrims on every road, for Spain, and for me, that my zeal may become charity, that I may walk faithfully with Christ, and that I may reach the end of the way. Amen.
penance: Walk somewhere today you would usually drive, offering it as a small pilgrimage, and pray for all who are on the Camino.
meditation: Can you drink the cup that I drink? James answered yes before he knew what it would cost. What is your answer today?
